9. The Madison Limestone aquifer contains ground water of fair to poor chemical suitability for potable use. Calcium sulfate is the principal constituent. Although this water has a high salinity, it may be utilized for agricultural purposes on soils of good permeability. Domestic users may require acclimation to minimize cathartic effects.
10. Relatively high ground-water temperatures may be found in these deeper aquifers. Concentrations of iron may also be present.
11. Ground water from the shallower aquifer formations is used mainly for domestic and agricultural purposes in the Tullock and Sarpy Creek drainages.
Various consultants retained by Westmoreland Resources have established ground water monitoring systems in the project area. Test well location's, and ground water quality data, as well as detailed descussion of these data are presented in Appendix D.
Aesthetics
Within the Westmoreland tracts and adjacent lands, the visually perceived characteristics are largely a function of the drainage networks, vegetation, outcrops, areas of steep terrain and related valleys, man-made structures and land use.
The landscape contained within the Westmoreland tracts is neither unique nor exceptionally representative of the larger surrounding physiographic region. Landscapes containing similar visual interest and integrity are present in abundance to the northeast, east and southeast of the site; more dramatic landscapes are found in the higher elevations
